描述_ZN: The Five Mountains, Ming dynasty, painted by Song Xu, on silk, 24.9 cm long, 75.9 cm wide.　　Shiqu Baoji Sequel, recorded in the Qianqing Palace, the eight seals of the whole Five Mountains, is the general name of the five famous mountains in China, referring to Mount Tai in the east, Mount Hua in the west, Mount Songshan in the middle, Mount Heng in the north, and Mount Heng in the south. The Five Mountains originated from the ancient Chinese worship of mountains and rivers, and were associated with the worship of mountain gods by the king of the country. The painting depicts the natural beauty of the five mountains, such as the sunny view of the sun, the clear autumn of Taihua, the two colors of the rushing peaks, the snowy Hengsei, and the two rooms of the mountain, using the technique of contrast between the light and the strong, the real and the imaginary to make the picture clear. In the composition, the artist uses the traditional flat and distant composition method, with the scenery near large and far small, near real and far virtual, with a strong sense of depth and distance. The brushwork is rough, elegant, and strong, with the sober and pale style of Shen Zhou's later paintings.　　The painting is recorded in the "Continued Compilation of Painting Treasures".
